spec.goal: A command-line tool, published on GitHub, that reads an accounting ledger CSV, applies five journal entry tests and writes an Excel workbook that supports fraud-risk triage by a human reviewer.
spec.expected_outcome: Running 'journal-entry-tests analyze ledger.csv --out-dir out' on a valid CSV produces out/results.xlsx with 8 sheets, exit code 0, and every planted problem in the test files appears as an alert.

criterion.metric: Recall of planted problems in the test file
criterion.measured_by: Automated recall test on the test file with planted problems

criterion.metric: Alerts from the four tests other than Benford on the clean test ledger
criterion.measured_by: Automated test on the clean test file

criterion.metric: Documented exit code cases handled correctly
criterion.measured_by: Automated test of the three exit cases
Automated test that opens the file and counts the sheets
Automated timed test on a 100000-row ledger
Manual review of the README against the checklist

checklist.item: Warning that an alert is a suspicion and not proof of fraud
LICENSE file with the MIT licence
Table of the input CSV format

role.needs: Triage of journal entries in a ledger that must not leave their computer.
role.permissions: Read the input CSV and write to the output folder.
Write to the repository and publish releases on GitHub.

spec.scope_in: The analyze command, CSV validation, five tests, aggregator, Excel workbook, English README, MIT licence, pytest tests and CI on GitHub Actions.
spec.scope_out: Synthetic data generator (lives in a separate private project, outside the public repository), Word report (optional future unit), graphical interface, server, database, PyPI publishing, multiple currencies, input formats other than CSV.

constraint.measured_by: Automated test that blocks sockets during analyze

constraint.threshold: exactly 2 of 2 Python versions green in CI, on Ubuntu and on Windows
constraint.measured_by: GitHub Actions run on 3.11 and 3.14, on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest

constraint.threshold: exactly 0 real records in the repository
constraint.measured_by: Manual review of the files in tests/fixtures before each release

spec.deadline: No deadline set by the owner.

assumptions.assumption: The ledger has a single currency; no conversion is done.
The ledger fits in memory (designed for up to 100000 rows).
The defaults (round base 1000, Benford minimum of 1000 rows) are reasonable for triage; they are configurable.

risks.risk: The newest NumPy and SciPy require Python 3.12 or later, so a pip freeze taken on 3.14 cannot install on 3.11; mitigation: constraints.txt with python_version markers, tested in CI.
The Nigrini thresholds were confirmed only in secondary sources.
The official ISA 240 text was not confirmed; the README cites only the topic.

Nigrini thresholds can flag ledgers near the minimum size even when they follow Benford (own simulation of 2000 runs per size: 2.25 percent flagged at 1000 rows, 1.0 percent at 1200, 0 percent at 5000); mitigation: caveat in the README and on the Benford sheet.
Someone using a result as proof of fraud; mitigation: warning in the README and in the workbook.

glossary.term: File with the accounting journal entries, one row per entry line.
Journal entry typed by a person and not generated by a system.
A row or group matching a test; it is a suspicion to review, not proof.
Mean absolute deviation between the observed and expected first digit distribution.
Amounts stored as integers in cents to avoid rounding errors.
CSV row that fails validation and goes to the Rejected rows sheet.
List of problems planted in a synthetic ledger, used by the tests.
Small synthetic file stored in tests/fixtures for the tests.
Line of the input CSV where a row starts, counting the header as line 1; identifies a row because entry_id may repeat.
Text identifier of a journal entry; may repeat across rows of the same entry.
Integer number of the source document, used by the numbering gaps test.
Row that passed validation; also called accepted row in the architecture.
Rows sharing the same account_code, signed amount and posting_date.
A range of missing integers between the minimum and maximum distinct document numbers.
An absolute amount of at least the round base that is a multiple of it.
An alert about the whole ledger, such as Benford, with no source_row.

spec.effort: Estimate: specification 4 h in total (about 2.5 h already done); build in five units by the AI, with about 1.5 h of owner reading and approval per unit, about 7.5 h. Available: 2 to 3 h per weekday and 5 to 6 h per weekend day. Fits in about 1 to 2 weeks. Estimate, not measured.
